processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The sample was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s.
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set temperature 950 °C at a rate of 5 °C/s (this sample's set T is 950 °C).
Held for 15 s at the set temperature (950 °C) before compression so the temperature difference between inside and outside of the sample was eliminated.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression to 60% (true strain 0.92) at a strain rate of 10 s^-1. Cylindrical sample Ø8 mm × 12 mm; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant applied to the end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression, the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down.

structures.overall_structure: Pre-deformation (as-forged billet) microstructure: large polygonal grains delimited by a bright, continuous, slightly etched boundary network enclosing dark grey grain interiors; within essentially every grain there are many fine, closely spaced, parallel light striations whose direction changes from grain to grain, giving strong segregation/dendritic-interdendritic banding (chemical heterogeneity) rather than a uniform solid solution.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; cylindrical sample Ø8 mm × 12 mm; mica foil + high-temperature lubricant on end faces
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900–1150 °C (this sample at 950 °C), strain rates 0.01–10 s^-1 (this sample 10 s^-1), max 60% compression (true strain 0.92)
characterization_methods.purpose: Study the hot deformation / rheological behaviour and dynamic recrystallization of the steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Flow (rheological) stress decreases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; steel is negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive.

characterization_methods.technique: optical metallography (laser confocal microscopy) of etched sections
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, prepared, ground, polished and etched; images with 100 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe microstructure evolution (deformation zones, DRX grains) and measure DRX average grain size
characterization_methods.key_findings: DRX degree greatest in the large-deformation zone and increases with temperature and decreasing strain rate; grain size increases with temperature and decreasing strain rate.

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine constitutive analysis with the Zener-Hollomon (Z) parameter
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fitted over the full experimental matrix T = 900–1150 °C, strain rates 0.01–10 s^-1; this sample is evaluated at 950 °C and 10 s^-1.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates strain rate, peak stress and temperature to determine the DRX activation energy
analytical_models.model_note: ε̇ = A[sinh(ασp)]^n exp(−Qp/RT). α determined as β/n1 = 0.00599.

analytical_models.equation_role: Computes activation energy from the average fitted slopes k1 and k2
analytical_models.model_note: Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2; value is an average over the experimental range because the fitted lines are not parallel.

analytical_models.equation_role: Temperature-compensated strain rate used to normalise flow-stress characteristic values
analytical_models.model_note: Z = ε̇·exp(Qp/RT). Table 1 reports lnZ for each (T, ε̇); for this sample (950 °C, 10 s^-1) lnZ = 68.18 (row 10 s^-1, column 950 °C).

computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear/nonlinear regression of DRX characteristic strains and stresses against lnZ
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Derived from flow-stress curves over T = 900–1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1 (Cingara-McQueen equation for critical strain)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Goodness-of-fit coefficients R reported: σc R=0.947, εc R=0.911, σp R=0.957, εp R=0.911, σs R=0.956, εs R=0.922

analytical_models.equation_role: Gives critical/peak/steady-state strains and stresses as functions of lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Models obtained by regression fitting; for this sample lnZ = 68.18. Also εc/εp ≈ 0.452 (Eq. 9, Cingara-McQueen). The specific characteristic values at 950 °C/10 s^-1 are not tabulated in the paper.

computational_details.simulation_method: Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation regression; finite-element (DEFORM-3D) framework referenced
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM-3D (finite element software referenced for numerical simulation of DRX average grain size)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet treated as rigid-plastic body, die as rigid; shear-type friction at billet-die interface = 0.3; convection coefficient billet-air = 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); semi-symmetric specimen; initial grain size and strain taken as fixed values
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% between predicted and experimental grain size; absolute error mostly within 3 µm

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts DRX average grain size as a function of strain rate and temperature

unmapped_findings: [Alloy/study-level, applicable to this sample's material but not a value specific to 950 °C/10 s^-1] The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ mol^-1, obtained from k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690 (Fig. 4); it is only an average value over the experimental range because the fitted lines are not parallel (b0032, b0034, b0085).

[Alloy/study-level] Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: rheological stress increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature (b0012, b0021, b0024, b0084).

[Alloy/study-level trend] The paper states that fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the range 950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C / 1–10 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086); this sample (950 °C/10 s^-1) falls in the low-T/high-ε̇ corner of the map, outside this optimum window.

[High strain rate group, includes this sample] At ε̇ = 10 s^-1 the peak stress decreases by 73% over 900–1150 °C, compared with an 82% reduction at 0.01 s^-1 (b0024); the specific peak stress at 950 °C/10 s^-1 is not tabulated in the paper.

No optical micrograph and no direct measured property value is reported specifically at 950 °C and 10 s^-1. The nearest reported micrograph is Fig. 9(d), which is 950 °C at 1 s^-1 (a different sample), showing banded/elongated structure with numerous large elongated remnant original grains and only locally fine recrystallized grains (b0063, figure_009).

DRX state diagram (Fig. 7, b0058) defines three zones in the lnZ–strain space: A = work hardening, B = partial DRX, C = complete DRX; both critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs increase with increasing lnZ (increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature), i.e. starting and completing DRX becomes more difficult.
